# Welcome {.unnumbered .unlisted}


This is the online version of **Applied Statistical
Methods for Health Sciences Research** by The rgtlab
Curriculum Project, a graduate textbook.

The book covers the applied methodological core of an
MS-level biostatistics curriculum. We begin with estimands
and study design and proceed to causal inference for
observational data, mediation, and longitudinal and
survival analysis at applied depth. We then take up
clinical trial design and analysis, missing-data
methodology, meta-analysis, and advanced categorical-data
methods. The volume sits between the workflow-focused
*Practicum* and the computing-focused *SCAI* volumes on
the methods axis.

The book sits in a five-volume graduate sequence:

- [*R for Biostatistics: A One-Week Boot Camp*](https://r-bootcamp.rgtlab.org)
, pre-program preparation.
- [*Biostatistics Practicum*](https://rgtlab.org/practicum)
, workflow infrastructure.
- [*Statistical Computing in the Age of AI*](https://scai.rgtlab.org)
, introductory methods and computing.
- [*Advanced Statistical Computing in the Age of AI*](https://scai-advanced.rgtlab.org)
, advanced numerical and Bayesian computation.
- [*Applied Generative AI for Health Sciences Research*](https://applied-genai.rgtlab.org)
, generative AI as the orthogonal axis.
- *Applied Statistical Methods for Health Sciences
  Research* (this volume), the applied-methods axis.

See the [Preface](preface.qmd) for motivation and the
[Conventions](conventions.qmd) page for visual cues.
